state.notes:
`@intentius/terragucci@0.4.63` on npm. Upgrade each repo with `npx @intentius/terragucci@0.4.63 init`, then merge the pipeline it writes.

terragucci is on chant `0.124.106`, in npm and in its images. Lexicons version apart from chant, so each bundled lexicon is pinned at its own latest release; prow and terraform are at `0.124.102`.

Prow's checkout has no `origin` remote. With `runtime: prow` each generated job now adds one that points at the GitHub the jobs post to, and the jobs that hold the token let git use it there. The apply job needs this to push its records to `chant/lifecycle`. The drift job now gets `TG_TOKEN`, which it keeps the drift issue with. chant's prow lexicon now writes the job config, and that move alone changes none of it. Run `npx @intentius/terragucci@0.4.63 init` to write the fixed jobs.

This is the first release tagged `v<version>`. Releases `0.4.50` to `0.4.62` were tagged `release/<version>`.

The [Changes page](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/whats-new/) lists every release.

state.notes:
`@intentius/terragucci@0.4.64` on npm. Upgrade each repo with `npx @intentius/terragucci@0.4.64 init`, then merge the pipeline it writes.

chant `0.124.112` is the pin for the package and the CI images.

`promotion: [dev, staging, prod]` in `terragucci.yml` names the order a release moves through the environments. `terragucci promote` applies a release to the next environment behind that environment's gate, and `terragucci rollback` brings an earlier release back the same way. `terragucci approve release <env>` approves a waiting one. A promote that skips an environment needs `--allow-skip`, and `--urgent --reason <text>` passes the stage's gate on its urgent rule with the reason on the stage's ledger. Each promote or rollback records the release the environment runs on `chant/lifecycle`. `init` writes `terragucci.component.ts`, which holds each root as one chant component. The merge applies the first stage and cuts the release that later stages promote; `release.cut: false` turns the cut off. [Promote a release through environments](https://intentius.io/terragucci/guides/promote-a-release/) walks through it.

Under `promotion`, `init` writes `release: { green: "forge-checks" }` into `chant.config.ts`, so the cut on merge waits for the merge commit's checks on the forge. On GitHub the wave jobs get the `checks`, `statuses` and `actions` read permissions for that. A pull request's plan runs in the first stage's environment, and its plan jobs and note jobs name that environment where they named `default`.

Each environment under `environments.<name>` takes chant's stage keys, such as `approval`, `approval_rules`, `hold`, `freeze`, `soak`, `canary`, `risk` and `hooks.<when>`; the [Stages](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/config/#stages) section lists them all. `terragucci ci` writes `.chant/pipeline.ts` from them, and `--check` fails on a stale file. A stage's first wave is its canary when `waves.canary` names every root in it and its soak has a check. `risk.approve_above` holds a wave over the score. The wave's risk record is `input.risk` in the policy and `waves[].risk` in the report. `terragucci reject`, `terragucci pause` and `terragucci resume` run chant's commands of those names.

`rollouts.soak` runs on chant's wave soak with its keys unchanged, and it also takes chant's `duration` and `checks` with `kind` and `on_fail`. A wave holds while a check finds drift, and the apply and policy checks hold it the same way. `/terragucci skip-soak` is recorded as the approval of the wave's soak gate with the commenter's name.

Agents start on a trigger, and each is off until its key is set. `agent.alert` answers a production alert and `agent.apply-failed` a failed apply. `agent.verify-failed` answers a failed verify or soak, and `agent.schedule` runs on a `cron`. `init` writes one workflow per agent beside the pipeline, and run records carry the `trigger`. The [agent from an alert guide](https://intentius.io/terragucci/guides/agent-start-from-an-alert/) points each alert source at chant's relay.

`terragucci.yml` reads the keys of chant's product vocabulary and still reads each earlier spelling. `gate: on-destructive` replaces `on-destroy`, and `identity` replaces `oidc`. `branches.<branch>` takes over from `apply.branches` and `forge_url` from `url`. `locks.when`, `drift.schedule` and `notify.relay_name` replace `locks`, `drift` and `notify.relay`. `terragucci config check` warns once for each earlier spelling it reads.

The cost estimate is chant's. chant runs `cost.command` (Infracost by default) over each root whose plan changes something and writes the cost section of the plan note, with a row per root. A root whose plan changes nothing is no longer priced. The command still reads the redacted plan from `TG_PLAN_JSON` and the root from `TG_ROOT`, and it still runs without the forge tokens. The `cost` keys in `terragucci.yml` are unchanged.

With `cost.approve_above`, the waves' spec carries chant's cost hold, which prices the wave, holds it over the amount and gives the `(monthly cost)` member of its digest. That member's digest is chant's now. The hold runs the command with chant's redaction, which covers what the plan marks sensitive, so declare each variable that takes a `secrets:` value `sensitive = true` ([Another estimator](https://intentius.io/terragucci/guides/estimate-cost/#another-estimator)). A wave that waited on its cost before the upgrade waits for an approval of its new digest, so approve it again with `terragucci approve`.

The policy's `input.cost` is chant's record, with fields such as `monthlyDelta`, `members` and `approveAbove`. The earlier fields `input.cost.root`, `input.cost.wave` and `input.cost.approve_above` sit beside them, so existing policies keep working. [Policy](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/policy/#cost) pairs each with chant's field. `run.cost_estimate` under `input: hcp` is filled as before.

`respond.wave-refused: summary` puts a model's summary above the diff in the note on a refused wave. chant's wave job runs it with the `agent.wave-refused` keys. [Have an agent summarize a refused wave](https://intentius.io/terragucci/guides/agent-refused-wave/#move-from-an-explain-refusal-job) shows how a repo with the `explain-refusal` job under `own_jobs` moves to it.

The reports bucket's files are in chant's report-store format, which every CI product on chant writes. `report.json` and `run.json` are `chant.run/v1`. `estate.json` is `chant.estate/v1` and `dora.json` is `chant.dora/v1`. Each names `product: "terragucci"` and keeps its body. Each new line of `audit.jsonl` is `chant.audit/v1`: chant's word for the event is in `kind` and terragucci's in `product_kind`. Lines already in the record stay as they are, and terragucci reads both forms. `index.json` stays `terragucci.report-index/v1`. [Reports bucket](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/reports-bucket/#json-schemas) lists the new ids, and the [audit trail](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/audit-trail/#query-the-record) has queries for the new lines.

The [Changes page](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/whats-new/) lists every release.

state.notes:
`@intentius/terragucci@0.4.65` on npm. Upgrade each repo with `npx @intentius/terragucci@0.4.65 init`, then merge the pipeline it writes.

chant moves to `0.124.115`, in the package and in the images it builds.

Each release now publishes the four CI images in two sets, eight in all. The package records the digest of every one. The Debian set is as before: `node:22-bookworm-slim`, apt, running as root. It runs Node `22.23.5`. The new Chainguard set is built on Chainguard's public `node` and `wolfi-base` images. It installs with apk and runs as user 65532. Its Node is the one Wolfi packages, `26.13.1` when the set was built, so a later release can move it to a newer major. Both sets carry the same engines at the same versions. The Chainguard tags end in `-chainguard` and share a repository with the Debian ones, and each image's labels record its base. The apk packages in the Chainguard images are installed at the versions chant pins, so they move with chant's pins.

`image.base` in `terragucci.yml` picks the set: `debian` (the default) or `chainguard`. `image: { base: chainguard }` is enough with no `name`, and `init` writes the pipeline with that set's image by digest. `image recipe` builds `FROM` the set `image.base` names. Its steps run as root and the image ends as the user the base runs as, so a layer of your own on the Chainguard base wraps its changes in `USER root` and `USER 65532` and installs with apk. [Run the jobs in a prepared image](https://intentius.io/terragucci/guides/run-in-a-prepared-image/#the-two-image-sets) and [Versions and pins](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/versions-and-pins/#the-two-image-sets) compare the two sets. A release before this one published only the Debian images and refuses `image.base: chainguard`.

terragucci's own release now runs with chant's `supply-chain` group on. It refuses a base image named without a digest and scans each image before anything is pushed. Each image gets an SBOM made from its layers and a keyless Sigstore signature. It also gets SLSA provenance, which the publish requires. The npm package carries an SBOM as well, and its scan covers the packages an install brings in, with no development dependencies.

The CI images move to engine releases built with a Go toolchain and Go modules that fix the critical vulnerabilities a scan finds in the older binaries:

| Engine | Was | Now | Image tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenTofu | `1.13.1` | `1.13.9` | `<version>-tofu1.13.9`, and `<version>-tg1.2.0-tofu1.13.9` for the Terragrunt image |
| Terraform | `1.14.9` | `1.17.2` | `<version>-tf1.17.2` |
| choudoufu | `0.31.0` | `0.35.0` | `<version>-choudoufu0.35.0` |
| Terragrunt | `1.2.0` | `1.2.0` | unchanged |

A root that pins its own version still runs that version, which the job installs. So a root that has to stay on Terraform `1.14.9` pins it in `.terraform-version` or `required_version`. The image build checks each new release against the sha256 terragucci records for it and against the release's checksums file.

The npm package's SBOM lists vitest `4` in place of vitest `3` and no longer lists tinypool `1.1.1`.

The [Changes page](https://intentius.io/terragucci/reference/whats-new/) lists every release.
